title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Spec Catalogue. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Spec Catalogue
options.lineage: 1990s Japanese car dealer brochures: halftone-screened photos, grade line-ups, ruled spec tables, cutaway drawings
options.thesis: Camilo published as this year's model: a printed spec catalogue for a person, where every claim is a row in a table and every photo is screened in dots.
materials: two-tone halftone and Atkinson dither screens
coated stock in Day, gunmetal ink in Dark
options.viewport: Cover spread: a tall plate holds Camilo's portrait dithered live in two inks with a cursor loupe that reveals true tone; beside it the name in wide extended capitals, a grade line, one honest line, a three-cell spec strip (Flagship MAGI / Base Pasto / Status open to work) and 'Download spec sheet (CV)'.
options.risk: Car-catalogue grammar could read as a car theme; it must stay print grammar (spec rows, grade plates, cutaways), never car pictures, or it tips into the game-UI feel you want to avoid.

raised.raise: No midtone anywhere: every screened image resolves to two inks with a hard edge, never a grey wash.
Spec tables are fixed-column ruled grids site-wide; columns never move, and the EN/ES toggle cascades values character by character in place.
Every row states its evidence: verified rows link to the repo, and missing material (testimonials, CV, demos) prints as an honest 'plate pending' slot, never filler.
Each project is a numbered plate in the line-up (No. 01 MAGI, No. 02 Ghost Layer) with catalogue margins, not a card in a grid.

options.label: 1-bit System
options.lineage: 1984 1-bit desktop computing: Atkinson-dithered pictures, pattern fills, bitmap type
options.thesis: The portfolio as a 1-bit desktop where dithering is native, because in that world it was the only way to show a photo.
options.viewport: A pattern-fill desktop with a window holding the dithered portrait, a Read Me window with the name, and a small CV window.
options.risk: The most familiar dither portfolio there is, and the desktop-OS metaphor drifts toward gimmick and game UI.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.thesis: ASCII taken literally: characters condense into Camilo's face, then blow apart into the words of the work.
options.viewport: An ASCII portrait made of drifting letters on white, the name as heavy matter, letters peeling off toward the project names.
options.case: Holds audience identification (your ASCII love, made the whole system); loses on clarity because words in motion fight a recruiter's ten-second scan.
options.risk: Constant letter motion is exactly the 'too noisy' failure if not held to one event per viewport.

options.label: Riso Zine
options.thesis: Camilo as a self-published riso zine: two fluorescent inks out of register, halftone grain where they cross.
options.viewport: Portrait screened in pink and blue a hair out of register, name overprinted in both inks, a yellow block holding the line.
options.case: Holds audience identification (halftone is your dither love in print); loses clarity because misregistered type softens reading and breaks the one-accent rule.
options.risk: Needs three inks, which breaks your single main colour, and the warm paper ground is a common default.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Projects and history as rows on a departure board.
options.viewport: A board of project rows flipping in.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in Camilo's world is a train station, and the board flattens the portrait.
options.kept: Fixed ruled columns that never move; values flip in place.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: Camilo's path as one ribbon of custody.
options.viewport: One ribbon running down the page through dated folds.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a student's two-year path is too short for a custody story.
options.kept: Known vs pending is always visible.

options.label: Cabaret Bill
options.thesis: The portfolio as tonight's programme in two harsh inks.
options.viewport: Angular portrait cut from black, programme leaning off the vertical.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no tie to Camilo's world, and leaning type hurts a fast scan.
options.kept: No midtone: lit or unlit with a hard edge.

options.label: Couture Atelier
options.case: Fuses poorly: the world has nothing to do with Camilo or engineering.
options.kept: Every item is a numbered plate with real margins.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dev portfolio everyone recognises, executed impeccably, with dither as accent tiles.
canonCard.viewport: Nav, avatar, name, one-line bio, CV button, a dithered tile beside it and a bento row of projects below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other dev portfolios by design, which is the 'generic dev template' you said would feel wrong.
